title: AuthorityTransition
description: The governed contract/state object for a durable mutation of human knowledge. Durable human knowledge changes ONLY through an AuthorityTransition. It is the architecture contract behind WriteGuard-equivalent runtime enforcement (app/write_guard.py) and the GovernedWriteProtocol (PolicyDecision -> DecisionToken -> AuthorityReceipt, docs/contracts/GOVERNED_WRITE_PROTOCOL.md): WriteGuard is the runtime mechanism, AuthorityTransition is the architecture state object. A persistence write is NOT an authority transition. Agent proposals are not mutations. Memory promotion, repair, and sync-conflict resolution that change semantic authority require a transition. Execution may not bypass it. After an accepted transition, DRI must invalidate/rebuild the affected derived representations.

actor_id.description: The actor (principal / delegated agent role) initiating the transition.

approved_authority_state.description: The authority_state actually granted by governance. Required once approval_state is approved; may differ from (be a downgrade of) requested_authority_state.

approval_required.description: Whether human/governance approval is required. Required true for promotion to durable/canonical authority unless an explicit policy exemption is referenced.

approval_exemption_policy_ref.description: Reference to the explicit policy that permits skipping approval for a promotion to canonical authority. Required when approval_required is false for such a promotion.

authority_receipt_id.description: AuthorityReceipt recording the governed decision. Required once approved; absent only while approval_state is not_required/pending/rejected/withdrawn.

decision_token_ref.description: GovernedWriteProtocol DecisionToken validated before the durable write (WriteGuard runtime tie-in).

promotion_request_id.description: The MemoryItem promotion request being materialized. Required when initiating_source is memory_promotion_request.

affected_derived_representation_ids.description: Derived/rebuildable representation IDs (segments, projections, indexes) that DRI must invalidate/rebuild after an accepted transition. Present (may be empty) so the rebuild obligation is explicit.

base_version.description: Version/revision the mutation is based on (optimistic-concurrency / conflict base).

result_version.description: Resulting version after an accepted transition.

conflict_state.description: Sync/merge conflict posture. Sync conflict resolution that changes semantic authority requires this transition; SFC stages, GOV decides.

rollback_ref.description: Reference enabling reversal of this transition where the operation class supports it.

allOf.$comment: An approval-EXEMPT promotion to durable/canonical authority skips human approval only — it is still an authority-bearing durable write, so it must reference the exemption policy AND carry the pre-mutation DecisionToken, the post-mutation AuthorityReceipt, and the granted authority state. Exemption never bypasses the GovernedWriteProtocol token+receipt invariant.

An approved transition carries the pre-mutation DecisionToken AND the post-mutation governance receipt, who/when approved, and the granted authority state. The DecisionToken requirement mirrors the GovernedWriteProtocol invariant (pre-mutation validation) so an approved transition cannot bypass governed-write enforcement.

Any transition that ACTUALLY grants accepted/canonical authority (via approved_authority_state) is an authority-bearing durable write and must carry the pre-mutation DecisionToken and post-mutation AuthorityReceipt — regardless of requested_authority_state or the approval path. Closes the gap where requested is lower but approved is canonical.

A completed no-approval (approval_state:not_required) transition that changes an object OUT OF accepted/canonical standing (e.g. deprecate, retract, correct of canonical knowledge) is still an authority-bearing durable write and must carry the DecisionToken and AuthorityReceipt. The destination-canonical guard does not cover downgrades out of canonical; the approved path is already covered by the approved-state guard.

Granting accepted/canonical authority without approval (approval_required:false) is an approval exemption and must reference the explicit exemption policy — even when only approved_authority_state (not requested_authority_state) is canonical.
Memory promotion transitions carry the originating promotion request id.
Consistency: if approval is required, the approval_state cannot be not_required.
Consistency: if approval is not required, the approval_state must be not_required (there is no pending/approved/rejected/withdrawn approval to record).

A non-grant approval state (pending / rejected / withdrawn) must carry NO grant artifacts: no approved_authority_state, approved_by, approved_at, decision_token_ref, or authority_receipt_id. Authority is materialized only when approval_state is `approved`, or via the approval_required:false exemption path (approval_state: not_required). This prevents a transition that is simultaneously rejected/pending and granting canonical.
